needs_human.note: A note's chip can now differ in case from its frontmatter from the moment it is registered: disk `python`, chip `Python`. The first chip edit rewrites the file to the row's spelling (frontend/src/lib/tags.ts:59-63), and a body-only save rewrites the row to the file's spelling (R2-F1). Which of the two wins depends on the next operation.; When one scan registers several notes with case variants of a new tag, the first note visited sets the row's spelling (test_scan_shares_new_tag_row_across_notes asserts only that the notes agree). The visiting order depends on the filesystem walk.; Registration projects only the first 10 valid tags (frontmatter.py:209-210), so a note with more shows only 10 chips, and the next chip edit writes that shorter list to the file. known-issues.md records this data loss for rejected tags but not for the cap.; Create parses the raw request body, so a CRLF frontmatter block is read as no frontmatter (frontmatter.py:110-112), while scan, upload and copy use read_text, which normalises line endings and projects it. Unchanged since the previous review.

Which spelling wins when a note's frontmatter differs in case from its shared row is declared differently by the user guide (first spelling kept) and the design rules (frontmatter canonical), and differs by path: registration keeps the row, PUT and Markdown bulk rename it.; project_frontmatter_tags' docstring at tagops.py:90 says 'Same rules as PUT /api/files/{id}/content', yet it passes respell=False while the PUT uses the default True.; Create parses the raw body (drives.py:1014, :1100) while scan, upload and copy parse read_text output, which normalises line endings. frontmatter.py:149 says parse treats a CRLF block as no frontmatter, so a CRLF note sent to create gets no tags, and over a missing row loses its old ones, where the same bytes uploaded project tags. Browser-entered text is expected to be LF, so this needs an API caller or pasted bytes; not run.

Three spelling rules now exist for one row: registration joins it as it stands, a move joins it as it stands through its own loop in `retarget_file_tags`, and a content PUT or internal post renames it. Whether a body-only save counts as a tag edit is not declared anywhere found.; A chip can differ from its own note's frontmatter spelling for as long as the note is not chip-edited, and a chip edit then rewrites the note's spelling on disk (decisions.md third run steps 1 and 3). Which of the two a reader should treat as correct is not declared beyond frontmatter being canonical.; A CRLF note is read through `read_text` on scan, upload and copy, which normalises line endings, so its tags are projected. `PUT content` parses the raw body, where `parse` reports no frontmatter (frontmatter.py:110-112), and `_write_md_tags` answers 422 (frontmatter.py:155-158). A CRLF note keeping its line endings can therefore get chips at registration and lose them on a raw save. An id write-back during a scan rewrites the file with LF, so this needs a note that already has an id or sits on a read-only drive.; On a read-only drive the tags now project, while `md_id` and `md_aliases` still do not, because the OSError return at scanner.py:319-320 precedes both, so one note ends up with a partial projection and no log line.
